questions.stem: Which type of joint allows for the most movement?
questions.explanation: Freely movable joints allow for a wide range of motion, unlike immovable or slightly movable joints.

distractorRationale.a: Immovable joints do not allow any movement, making them unsuitable for mobility.
distractorRationale.b: Slightly movable joints provide limited movement, which is less than that of freely movable joints.
distractorRationale.c: Fixed joints are essentially the same as immovable joints, providing no flexibility.

questions.stem: What is a characteristic feature of synovial joints?

options.text: They are found only in the skull.

distractorRationale.c: Ligaments are essential for the stability of synovial joints, so they must be present.

distractorRationale.b: Pectorals and deltoids are not antagonistic muscles; they work on different movements.
distractorRationale.c: Gastrocnemius and soleus are related to ankle movement, not the elbow.

questions.stem: Which type of joint is found in the skull and allows no movement?
questions.explanation: Immovable joints, also known as fixed joints, do not allow any movement between the bones. They are primarily found in the skull, where the bones are tightly fused together for protection.

distractorRationale.a: Hinge joints allow movement in one direction, such as at the elbow.
distractorRationale.b: Ball and socket joints allow for a wide range of movement, such as in the shoulder.
distractorRationale.d: Saddle joints allow movement in two planes but are not immovable.

questions.stem: What is the primary role of synovial fluid in a joint?

options.text: To provide nutrients to the bone

questions.explanation: Synovial fluid serves to lubricate the joint, reducing friction between the articular cartilages during movement. This lubrication is essential for smooth and pain-free motion.

distractorRationale.a: Synovial fluid does not provide nutrients to bones; it mainly aids in lubrication.
distractorRationale.c: Muscles are connected to bones by tendons, not synovial fluid.
distractorRationale.d: While synovial fluid helps in movement, it does not strengthen the joint.

questions.stem: Which part of the synovial joint acts as a cushion between the bones?

distractorRationale.a: The synovial membrane produces synovial fluid but does not cushion the bones.
distractorRationale.c: The joint capsule encases the joint but does not provide cushioning.
distractorRationale.d: Ligaments connect bones to other bones but do not cushion the joint.

questions.stem: What type of movement occurs at the elbow joint when the biceps contract?
questions.explanation: When the biceps contract, they pull the forearm up towards the shoulder, resulting in flexion at the elbow joint. This action decreases the angle between the forearm and the upper arm.

distractorRationale.a: Extension occurs when the triceps contract, not the biceps.
distractorRationale.c: Rotation is a different type of movement not associated with the biceps at the elbow.
distractorRationale.d: Abduction refers to movement away from the midline and is not applicable to the elbow joint.
